# Mass and size {#sec-dd-mass}


::: {.cell}

:::


## Overview

These columns give the vehicle's mass in kilograms and, for cars, the size
of its model.

The revenue weight (the DVLA's name for it) is the vehicle's maximum
permitted gross mass in kilograms, as the DVLA records it. It matters most
for goods vehicles and buses, which are classed by mass.

- **`revenue_weight`** is the harmonised revenue weight: the DVLA value where the VES
  record describes this vehicle, otherwise the most common value among
  vehicles of the same make, model, birth year, fuel and engine size, and
  failing that of the same make, model, birth year and fuel.
- **`revenue_weight_src`** says which (`dvla`, `variant` or
  `model_year_fuel`).
- **`revenueWeight_DVLA`** is the value as supplied.

The backfill is described in the methodology,
[section 5.6](../../reports/methodology.md#other-attributes).

For cars, the mass and dimensions of the car's model are also linked from
the RACF car fleet (@sec-dd-racf). They are averages for the model, year and
fuel, not measurements of the car, and are blank for vehicles that are not
cars.

- **`mass_kg`** is the EU mass in running order: the empty car with its fluids,
  a 90% full tank and a 75 kg driver. **`kerb_weight_kg`** is the Dutch RDW
  register's kerb mass. Both are well below the revenue weight, which is the
  maximum permitted mass of the loaded car.
- **`length_mm`**, **`width_mm`** and **`height_mm`** are the RDW dimensions,
  **`wheelbase_mm`** the wheelbase, and **`footprint_m2`** the EU footprint,
  the wheelbase times the track, in m².

## Coverage

The revenue weight is the least complete of the DVLA attributes. The DVLA records it
for only 30% of vehicles, even though a VES
record was found for far more, and most of those with a value were first used
since 2010 (@fig-dd-mass). The backfill raises coverage to
70%, but only to
47% for vehicles first used before
2000, as few similar vehicles of that age have a recorded value to copy.

Because most values are filled rather than recorded, check results that
depend on mass against the recorded values only
(`revenue_weight_src = 'dvla'`; @sec-pitfalls).

The RACF columns are present only for cars whose model was linked and whose
linked RACF rows have a plausible value. The EU mass and footprint and the RDW
kerb mass are present for most cars: `mass_kg` for
74% of all vehicles. The RDW length and width are
present for fewer (`length_mm` for 51%), as fewer
models were matched to those fields of the register.

## Values

How the values of each column change over time, by year of first use, from
1990. Numeric columns show the minimum, lower quartile (Q1), median, upper
quartile (Q3) and maximum; other columns show the share of vehicles with each
value, with the less common values grouped as *All other values* and missing
values as *Blank*.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

### `revenue_weight`

Revenue weight, the maximum permitted gross mass (kg): DVLA (same vehicle only), else the most common value of vehicles with the same make/model/birth year/fuel/engine size (variant), else of the same make/model/birth year/fuel (model_year_fuel); see revenue_weight_src.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}

:::
:::
